content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).
content.topic: 掌握基础知识对学好一门学科至关重要

modelEssay.title: The Importance of Mastering the Basics
modelEssay.content:
As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject. Without a solid grasp of fundamental concepts, even the most ambitious learner will find advanced study an uphill battle.

There are at least two reasons why the basics deserve our undivided attention. First, fundamental knowledge serves as the foundation upon which the entire edifice of a discipline is built. A student of physics, for instance, who fails to understand Newton's laws will inevitably struggle when confronted with quantum mechanics. Second, mastering the basics cultivates the analytical habits and confidence that allow learners to tackle complex problems independently rather than memorising answers mechanically.

In light of the above, I firmly believe that students should resist the temptation to rush ahead and instead devote sufficient time to consolidating what is elementary. Only by building on a firm foundation can we reach greater academic heights.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：以给定首句点题，指出缺乏基础将使深入学习举步维艰。
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：从“基础是学科大厦的根基”和“掌握基础培养独立分析能力与信心”两方面论证。
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：呼应主题，呼吁学生沉下心夯实基础，方能攀登学术高峰。

the foundation upon which the entire edifice of a discipline is built（学科大厦的根基）
cultivates the analytical habits and confidence（培养分析习惯与信心）

transcript.text: Conversation One.

transcript.text: Hello, Doctor.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你好，医生。

transcript.text: Hello, please take a seat. I have your test results here, and it's good news. The blood test came back clear. There is no indication of any digestive issues.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你好，请坐。我这里有你的检查结果，是个好消息。血液测试结果正常，没有显示任何消化系统问题。

transcript.text: So then, why do I feel so poorly all the time?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 那为什么我一直感觉这么不舒服呢？

transcript.text: It's probably due to overwork and stress.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 可能是由于过度劳累和压力。

transcript.text: No, it can't be. I've always been working hard, but I've never felt stress. Other people suffer and complain about that, but I don't. It must be something else.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 不，不可能。我一直努力工作，但从未感到过压力。其他人受苦并抱怨那个，但我不。一定是其他原因。

transcript.text: What you have just described is a common sentiment. Many people who suffer from stress fail to recognise it. You told me you often work long into the night, right?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 你刚才描述的是一种常见的感受。许多承受压力的人没有意识到它。你告诉我你经常工作到深夜，对吧？

transcript.text: Yes, most days in fact. But I've been doing that for about 20 years now.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，事实上大多数日子都是。但我这样做已经大约20年了。

transcript.text: That doesn't matter. You could have been suffering from stress for 20 years without knowing it, and now it's catching up to you.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 那没关系。你可能已经承受了20年的压力而不自知，现在它开始显现了。

transcript.text: But what about my feeling tired all the time and not being able to sleep well at night?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 但我一直感到疲倦和晚上睡不好怎么办？

transcript.text: Those are common consequences of stress. And if you don't sleep well, then of course you will feel fatigued. I'm going to prescribe some special sleeping pills for you. They have a soft, gentle effect and are made from natural ingredients, so your stomach should tolerate them fine, and there shouldn't be any negative side effects. Take one with your dinner and come see me after a month. If there is no improvement, I'll give you something stronger.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这些是压力的常见后果。如果你睡不好，当然会感到疲倦。我会给你开一些特殊的安眠药。它们有温和的效果，由天然成分制成，所以你的胃应该能很好耐受，不会有副作用。晚餐时服一粒，一个月后来看我。如果没有改善，我会给你更强的药。

transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 谢谢你，医生。

transcript.text: That's not all. You should try and work less. Is there any way you can decrease your workload?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 还不止这些。你应该试着少工作。有没有办法减少你的工作量？

transcript.text: I'd have to think about it. I'm a restaurant manager, and this industry is very competitive. There are many things to keep track of and stay on top of.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我得考虑一下。我是一名餐厅经理，这个行业竞争非常激烈。有很多事情需要跟踪和处理。

transcript.text: I recommend you think about delegating some responsibilities to someone else. I'm not asking you to retire, just to slow down a bit. It's for your own health.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我建议你考虑将一些责任委托给其他人。我不是要你退休，只是稍微放慢一点。这是为了你自己的健康。

transcript.translation: 对话二。

transcript.text: Today on People in the News, our guest is John Williams. The name may not sound familiar to you, but John was once an acclaimed basketball player. John, you stunned fans by leaving the sport at just 25. Why did you retire so early?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 今天的《新闻人物》，我们的嘉宾是约翰·威廉姆斯。这个名字你可能不太熟悉，但约翰曾经是一位备受赞誉的篮球运动员。约翰，你在25岁就离开这项运动，令球迷们震惊。你为什么这么早退役？

transcript.text: Meg, I loved being an athlete, but I didn't love being a celebrity. I was in the limelight when I was still a high school student and went professional right after high school graduation, which was a mistake. I was a shy kid and I wasn't ready for all the media attention.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 梅格，我喜欢当运动员，但我不喜欢成为名人。我还是高中生时就在聚光灯下，高中毕业后直接转为职业球员，这是一个错误。我是个害羞的孩子，还没有准备好应对所有媒体的关注。

transcript.text: But walking away from millions of dollars at the height of your career, most people wouldn't be able to resist the lure of such a high salary. When you left the sport, there was speculation that you were having issues with your teammates or even an injury.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: Not at all. It was hard to quit. I was tempted to stay in the game because I loved basketball and I loved my team. As for money, I turned professional at 18, so I'd actually earned a lot and saved most of it because I had great financial advisors. I knew basketball wasn't a career with a lot of longevity for most players, so I wanted to change careers while I was still young.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 完全不是。放弃很难。我曾被诱惑留在比赛中，因为我热爱篮球和我的球队。至于钱，我18岁就转为职业球员，所以我实际上赚了很多，并且存了大部分，因为我有优秀的财务顾问。我知道篮球对大多数球员来说不是职业生涯很长的运动，所以我想趁年轻转行。

transcript.text: Okay, that was 20 years ago and you're back in the news. You've created a foundation that works to get more kids playing team sports. Why?
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 好吧，那是20年前的事了，你又回到了新闻中。你创建了一个基金会，致力于让更多孩子参与团队运动。为什么？

transcript.text: I went to university and I studied public health and learned about the seriousness of the obesity epidemic, particularly among kids and adolescents in poor communities. I've spent the last two decades trying to alleviate the problem. The foundation is just the latest attempt.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我上了大学，学习公共卫生，了解到肥胖流行病的严重性，特别是在贫困社区的孩子和青少年中。过去二十年，我一直在努力缓解这个问题。基金会只是最新的尝试。

transcript.translation: 第一段。

transcript.text: Kate Atkinson was born in York, England in 1951. She worked hard to gain her credentials as an author. She studied English literature at university in Scotland. After graduating in 1974, she researched a doctorate on American literature. Later, she taught at the university she graduated from and began writing short stories in 1981. She began writing for women's magazines after winning the 1986 Women's Own Short Story Competition.
transcript.translation: 凯特·阿特金森于1951年出生在英格兰的约克。她努力工作，获得了作为作家的资格。她在苏格兰的大学学习英国文学。1974年毕业后，她研究美国文学的博士学位。后来，她在她毕业的大学任教，并于1981年开始创作短篇小说。在赢得1986年《女性自己》短篇小说比赛后，她开始为女性杂志撰稿。

transcript.text: Her first novel, Behind the Scenes at the Museum, won the 1995 UK Book of the Year award. The book is set in Yorkshire and has been adapted for radio, theatre and TV. She has written two plays for a theatre in Edinburgh. The first was called Nice and the second, Abandonment, performed as part of the Edinburgh Festival in August 2000.
transcript.translation: 她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》赢得了1995年英国年度图书奖。该书以约克郡为背景，并已被改编为广播、戏剧和电视节目。她为爱丁堡的一家剧院写了两部戏剧。第一部名为《尼斯》，第二部名为《遗弃》，于2000年8月作为爱丁堡艺术节的一部分上演。

transcript.text: Whatever genre Atkinson writes in, her books touch on the themes of love and loss and how to carry on. They are always presented with ingenuity and a wicked sense of humour. Her books tend to be populated by odd, sometimes sinful and generally flawed eccentrics, who become credible by virtue of being so fully realised. Her books have frequently been described as comedies of manners, that is to say, comedies that represent the complex and sophisticated code of behaviour current in fashionable circles of society, where appearances count more than true moral character. A comedy of manners tends to reward its clever and deceitful characters rather than punish their bad deeds. The humour of a comedy of manners relies on verbal wit and playful teasing.
transcript.translation: 无论阿特金森写何种体裁，她的书都触及爱与失去以及如何继续前行的主题。它们总是以巧妙和一种顽皮的幽默感呈现。她的书往往充斥着古怪、有时罪恶且通常有缺陷的怪人，由于刻画得如此充分而变得可信。她的书常被描述为风俗喜剧，即反映时尚社交圈中复杂而精致的行为准则的喜剧，在那里外表比真正的道德品格更重要。风俗喜剧倾向于奖赏其聪明狡猾的角色，而不是惩罚他们的恶行。风俗喜剧的幽默依赖于语言机智和 playful teasing。

transcript.text: Passage Two.
transcript.translation: 第二段。

transcript.text: Why is adaptability an important skill to exercise in the workplace? Simply put, adaptability is a skill employers are increasingly looking for. When you spend time learning a new task rather than resisting it, your productivity goes up. You can also serve as an example to your co-workers who may be having trouble adapting, and can help lead your team forward.
transcript.translation: 为什么适应力是在工作场所中运用的一项重要技能？简而言之，适应力是雇主日益寻求的一种技能。当你花时间学习一项新任务而不是抵制它时，你的生产力会提高。你还可以为那些可能难以适应的同事树立榜样，并帮助引领你的团队前进。

transcript.text: Strategy consultant Dory Clark explains it to us this way. I'd say that adaptability is an important skill in the workplace because, frankly, circumstances change. Competitors introduce new products. The economy might enter a recession. Customer preferences differ over time. If you shake your fist at the sky and say, why can't it stay the same, that's not going to do very much good.
transcript.translation: 战略顾问Dory Clark这样向我们解释。我认为适应力在工作场所中是一项重要技能，因为坦率地说，情况会变化。竞争对手推出新产品。经济可能进入衰退。顾客的偏好随时间而不同。如果你向天空挥拳并说，为什么它不能保持不变，那不会有多大帮助。

transcript.text: Instead, you need to recognise when circumstances have changed so you can take appropriate action based on what is, rather than how you wish the world would be. That enables you to make more accurate, informed and effective choices. Also, the workplace itself has been evolving. Today's work culture and management style is often based on teamwork rather than a rigid hierarchy. Brainstorming, which requires creativity, flexibility and emotional intelligence, is a typical problem-solving technique.
transcript.translation: 相反，你需要认识到情况何时变化，以便你能根据实际情况采取适当行动，而不是基于你希望世界如何。这使你能够做出更准确、更知情和更有效的选择。此外，工作场所本身也在演变。当今的工作文化和管理风格往往基于团队合作，而不是僵化的层级制度。头脑风暴，需要创造力、灵活性和情商，是一种典型的问题解决技巧。

transcript.text: Employees who are unable or unwilling to participate will not easily move forward in the company. Employees who are flexible demonstrate other skills too. They can re-prioritise quickly when changes occur and suggest additional modifications when something's not working. They can also regroup quickly when a setback occurs, adapting to the new situation confidently and without overreacting.
transcript.translation: 不能或不愿参与的员工在公司中不易晋升。灵活的员工也展示了其他技能。当变化发生时，他们能快速重新确定优先级，并在某些事情不起作用时建议额外的修改。当遇到挫折时，他们也能迅速重新组合，自信地适应新情况，而不是过度反应。

transcript.text: What makes humans different from other species? Some philosophers argue it's morals or ethics, while some scientists assert it's our greater cognitive development. But I argue that the main difference is our desire to combat routine. This makes being creative a biological mandate, as what we seek in art and technology is surprise, not simply a fulfilment of expectations. As a result, a wild imagination has characterised the history of our species.
transcript.translation: 人类与其他物种的区别是什么？一些哲学家认为是道德或伦理，而一些科学家则断言是我们更高的认知发展。但我认为主要区别在于我们对抗常规的欲望。这使得创造力成为一种生物学上的必然，因为我们在艺术和技术中寻求的是惊喜，而非仅仅是期望的满足。因此，狂野的想象力一直是我们物种历史的特征。

transcript.text: We build intricate habitats, devise complex recipes for our food, wear clothes that reflect constant changes in fashion, communicate with elaborate signs, symbols and sounds, and travel between habitats on wings and wheels of our own design. To satisfy our appetite for novelty, innovation is key. But who innovates? Now, many people, both laymen and experts, believe that only geniuses innovate.
transcript.translation: 我们建造复杂的栖息地，为食物设计复杂的配方，穿着反映时尚不断变化的衣服，用精细的符号、标志和声音进行交流，并在我们自己设计的翅膀和轮子之间穿梭于栖息地之间。为了满足我们对新奇的渴望，创新是关键。但谁在创新呢？现在，许多普通人和专家都认为只有天才才能创新。

transcript.text: But I believe that innovation is not something that only a few people do. The innovative drive lives in every human brain, and the resulting war against the repetitive is what powers the massive changes that distinguish one generation from the next. The drive to create the new is a trait of being human. We build cultures by the hundreds and tell new stories by the millions. We create and surround ourselves with things that have never existed before, while animals do not.
transcript.translation: 但我相信创新不是只有少数人才做的事情。创新动力存在于每个人的大脑中，由此产生的对抗重复的战争推动了巨大的变化，这些变化区分了一代人与下一代人。创造新事物的动力是人类的特质。我们创造数以百计的文化，讲述数以百万计的新故事。我们创造并用从未存在过的事物包围自己，而动物则不然。

transcript.text: But where do our new ideas come from? According to many, new ideas come from seemingly nowhere, to great minds. From this perspective, new ideas are almost like magic. They come in a flash of inspiration to a select few. However, the reality is that, across the spectrum of human activities, prior work propels the creative process. We may think of innovation as being the result of inspiration or genius, but it's really the result of developing the ideas of others further.
transcript.translation: 但我们的新想法从何而来？许多人认为，新想法对伟大的头脑来说似乎凭空而来。从这个角度看，新想法几乎像魔法一样。它们在灵感的闪现中降临到少数人身上。然而，现实是，在人类活动的各个领域，先前的工作推动着创造性过程。我们可能认为创新是灵感或天才的结果，但它实际上是进一步发展他人想法的结果。

transcript.text: This happens in technology, where one invention enables or inspires further inventions. And it happens in the arts, as writers, composers, and painters use the work of previous artists in their own work. The human brain works from precedent. We take the ideas we've inherited and put them together into some new shape. What is a true creator? Is a creator a genius who makes something out of nothing? No. Creators are simply humans who use what they inherit, who absorb the past and manipulate it to create possible futures. Thus, humans are creators as a rule, rather than as an exception.
transcript.translation: 这在技术领域发生，一项发明促使或启发进一步的发明。在艺术领域也是如此，作家、作曲家和画家在他们的作品中使用先前艺术家的作品。人类大脑基于先例工作。我们把继承的想法组合成新的形状。什么是真正的创造者？创造者是凭空创造的天才吗？不。创造者只是使用他们所继承的东西，吸收过去并操纵它来创造可能的未来的普通人。因此，人类作为创造者是常态，而非例外。

transcript.text: Many dog owners will tell you that their dog somehow knows when they're ill or upset. And, according to researchers who study dog cognition, those pet owners are right. Dogs do know when their human companions are having a rough time. Not only can your dog sense when you have a cold, but domestic dogs have shown an aptitude for detecting both much smaller mood fluctuations and far more serious physical conditions. This is because dogs are extremely sensitive to changes in the people they're familiar with, and illness causes change.
transcript.translation: 许多狗主会告诉你，他们的狗不知怎的知道他们何时生病或难过。而且，根据研究狗认知能力的学者，这些宠物主人是对的。狗确实知道它们的人类伴侣何时处于困境。你的狗不仅能察觉你是否感冒，家犬还表现出检测更微小的情绪波动以及远为严重的身体状况的能力。这是因为狗对它们所熟悉的人身上的变化极为敏感，而疾病会引起变化。

transcript.text: If a person is infected with a virus or bacteria, for example, their odour will be abnormal, and dogs are able to smell that change even if the human can't, because dogs have a much more powerful sense of smell than humans. Researchers have also found that a person's mood, which can be an indicator of a larger illness, triggers a dog's sense of smell. Human emotions manifest physically in chemical signals that are emitted by the body, and dogs are able to smell those as well.
transcript.translation: 例如，如果一个人感染了病毒或细菌，他们的气味就会异常，而狗能够嗅出这种变化，即使人类无法察觉，因为狗的嗅觉比人类强大得多。研究人员还发现，一个人的情绪——这可能是更重大疾病的征兆——也会触发狗的嗅觉。人类的情绪通过身体发出的化学信号在生理上显现，狗也能嗅到这些信号。

transcript.text: Beyond smell, dogs gather information from a person's voice in order to sense changes. In 2014, researchers discovered that dogs have an area of the brain similar to one in humans that allows them to understand emotional cues in the tone of a speaker's voice, beyond what they'd be able to pick up from familiar words alone. A person's voice can also carry indicators of illness. What's not understood quite so well is what dogs understand about these changes.
transcript.translation: 除了嗅觉，狗还通过人的声音收集信息以感知变化。2014年，研究人员发现，狗的大脑中有一个类似于人类的区域，使它们能够理解说话者声音语调中的情绪线索，而不仅仅是通过熟悉的词汇来理解。一个人的声音也可能携带疾病的迹象。目前理解得不太清楚的是，狗对这些变化究竟了解多少。

transcript.text: Humans send out lots of cues, but whether dogs know some of these cues mean illness isn't clear. What we perceive as concern on a dog's part might be more like increased curiosity or suspicion that something is wrong with us, and sticking close by is a great way to gather more information about the situation. Some researchers assert dogs will one day help doctors diagnose diseases, as some dogs have already demonstrated the ability to detect an assortment of ailments, including diabetes and certain types of cancer. But those researchers concede that's probably in the distant future. For now, research suggests dog ownership can have an array of benefits in and of itself. Keeping a pet dog has been shown to bolster health and boost mood. Dogs also help people relax, and they can be a particular comfort to those with chronic diseases.
transcript.translation: 人类会发出许多信号，但狗是否知道其中一些信号意味着疾病尚不清楚。我们认为的狗表现出的关切，可能更像是增加的好奇心或怀疑我们出了什么问题，而紧跟着是收集更多关于情况信息的好方法。一些研究人员认为，狗终有一天会帮助医生诊断疾病，因为有些狗已经展现出检测多种疾病的能力，包括糖尿病和某些类型的癌症。但这些研究人员承认，那可能是在遥远的未来。目前，研究表明养狗本身就有一系列好处。养宠物狗已被证明能增强健康、提振情绪。狗还能帮助人们放松，对患有慢性疾病的人来说尤其是一种安慰。

transcript.text: Earlier this month, the think tank called Onward published a report, A Question of Degree, which argues that degrees in the creative arts are not good value for money. Ministers, according to Onward, should crack down on courses that offer extremely limited value for money to students 10 years after graduation, restricting the ability of such courses to recruit new students if the average graduate earns below the student loans payment threshold. Courses like science, technology, engineering and maths, and economics, where the average graduate earns a lot, should be favoured. The report provides insight into a government review which looks at how to reform technical education and how to ensure students get good value for money.
transcript.translation: 本月早些时候，名为Onward的智库发布了一份报告《学位之问》，其中指出创意艺术学位性价比不高。根据Onward的说法，部长们应该打击那些在学生毕业10年后提供极低性价比的课程，如果毕业生平均收入低于学生贷款还款门槛，就限制这些课程招收新学生的能力。像科学、技术、工程和数学以及经济学等毕业生平均收入较高的课程应受到青睐。该报告为一项政府审查提供了见解，该审查着眼于如何改革技术教育以及如何确保学生获得物有所值的教育。

transcript.text: At first glance, it might even seem like Onward have a point. According to their data, the majority of creative arts students earn less than 25,000 pounds a year, 10 years after graduation. The average male creative arts students, indeed, apparently earn much less than they would had they simply never gone to university. This isn't really good for anyone, and it's certainly no good for graduates, who are forced to endure a lifestyle where they can never save up, never buy a house, never hope to retire.
transcript.translation: 乍一看，Onward似乎有道理。根据他们的数据，大多数创意艺术学生在毕业10年后年收入低于25,000英镑。事实上，男性创意艺术学生的平均收入显然远低于他们从未上过大学的情况。这对任何人都不好，对毕业生尤其不利，他们被迫忍受一种永远无法储蓄、永远买不起房、永远无法指望退休的生活方式。

transcript.text: Onward have identified a real problem. But creative arts graduates from top universities like Oxford, with a high proportion of privately educated students, have fairly good work prospects, while 40% of all graduates, regardless of their degree, are on less than 25,000 pounds a year, 5 years after graduation. This suggests that the problem isn't really to do with specific students studying specific degrees, but really with the economy as a whole.
transcript.translation: Onward发现了一个真正的问题。但像牛津这样拥有高比例私立教育学生的顶尖大学的创意艺术毕业生，工作前景相当不错，而所有毕业生中，无论其学位如何，40%的人在毕业5年后年收入低于25,000英镑。这表明问题实际上与特定学生学习特定学位无关，而是与整体经济有关。

transcript.text: Regardless of what they've studied, young people find it hard to get ahead, unless they're lucky enough to be born with successful parents. If ministers want to make education pay for young people, they need to look beyond the higher education sector, towards the wider world. The rewards that education gives us are not measurable. They are not always instantly obvious, and certainly not always direct. And education makes you a different person from the one you would have been if you hadn't received it. We need to look at the value of education not in the context of a bank balance, but of a life. If we continue to allow ourselves to be distracted with talk of value for money, we will all be made poorer as a result.
transcript.translation: 无论他们学了什么，年轻人发现很难取得成功，除非他们幸运地出生在有成功父母的家庭。如果部长们想让教育对年轻人有回报，他们需要超越高等教育领域，看向更广阔的世界。教育给予我们的回报是不可衡量的。它们并不总是立即显现，当然也并不总是直接的。教育使你成为如果你没有接受教育就不会成为的人。我们需要审视教育的价值，不是基于银行账户余额，而是基于生活。如果我们继续让自己被性价比的讨论分散注意力，结果是我们都会变得更贫穷。

paragraphs.translation: 然而，像所有沙漠一样，如果你有耐心，你将获得回报，因为它们常常缓慢地揭示秘密。在我最近一次出行中，我惊讶地发现该地区有多少是由古代火山和地质力量塑造的，其中大部分至今仍保留，赋予该地区独特的感觉，并为精彩的照片绘制了丰富多彩的背景。

questionGroups.title: African countries must get smarter with their agriculture

material.title: African countries must get smarter with their agriculture

paragraphs.text: On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. "The rainy season is no longer predictable," says one. "When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once." Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. "Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts," says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds.
paragraphs.translation: 在肯尼亚中部的山丘上，阳光照耀下的茶树丛闪烁着近乎柠檬绿的光芒，农民们对气候变化了如指掌。"雨季不再可预测，"一位农民说。"该下雨的时候不下雨，然后所有雨水一涌而至。"气候变化是一个将影响地球上每个人的问题。对非洲人来说，其后果将尤为痛苦：其他地区通过燃烧煤炭和石油得以致富，而非洲将在未享受这些益处的情况下付出巨大的人力代价。"非洲仅占全球温室气体排放的2%，但它是预计受气候影响最严重的大陆，"世界银行80亿美元气候投资基金的负责人马法尔达·杜阿尔特说。

paragraphs.text: Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5℃, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize (玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18-22%.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管气候变化的确切影响存在巨大不确定性，但已有足够证据表明全球变暖是非洲繁荣面临的主要威胁之一。该大陆的部分地区升温速度已远高于平均水平：过去50年间，南部非洲的气温上升速度约为全球平均水平的两倍。即使全球减排足够将升温控制在1.5℃以下，非洲的热浪仍将加剧，疾病将传播到目前未受影响的地区。农业也将受到严重打击。目前用于种植玉米的土地中约40%将不再适宜种植。总体而言，预计玉米产量将下降18%至22%。

paragraphs.text: Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.
paragraphs.translation: 非洲尤其脆弱，部分原因是它已经在努力养活自己，而即使没有气候变化，它也必须大幅提高产量和生产力，才能满足快速增长人口的食物需求。联合国粮食及农业组织估计，到2050年，全球粮食产量需比2009年水平增长约70%，以满足人口增长和需求增长。大部分新需求将来自非洲。然而，该大陆每年进口价值约500亿美元的食品，且这一数字预计将在未来五年内翻倍以上。自给自足并非非洲的目标，但其进口食品的花费超过购买资本货物的事实表明，它仍有改进空间。

paragraphs.text: Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.
paragraphs.translation: 找出原因并不难。大多数农场面积小，依靠手工耕作和雨水。超过一半的非洲人口以农业为生。尽管过去几十年总收获量有所上升，但这主要是因为更多人耕种了更多土地。但在许多地方没有闲置土地可耕种。卢旺达的地块小到你可以在一个美国农场里容纳250个这样的地块。尽管过去30年非洲的人均产出增长了超过一半，但仍远落后于亚洲2.5倍的增长。玉米产量通常低于每公顷两吨，仅为美国水平的五分之一。

paragraphs.text: The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. "They can't even feed their families," says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. "Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years."
paragraphs.translation: 非洲农民的低生产率反映在国民经济统计中——尽管吸收了如此多劳动力，农业仅贡献了15%的GDP。"他们甚至无法养活自己的家庭，"负责农业的非洲开发银行副总裁詹妮弗·布兰克说。"在非洲许多地区，农业生产率在100年来没有改善。"

paragraphs.text: One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa (可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum (高梁), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.
paragraphs.translation: 原因之一是，在独立后的最初几十年里，许多非洲政府忽视农业，专注于经济工业化。其他国家则通过压低国家垄断企业支付给农民的作物价格来损害农业，以用廉价食品补贴城市工人。加纳对可可出口征收重税，导致在1960年代至1980年代间产量下降了一半，尽管全球可可价格飙升。然而，在过去二十年左右，政府和捐助者开始重新审视农业，将其作为每年为1300万进入劳动力市场的年轻人提供就业的一种方式。大部分重点放在让小农使用化肥，更重要的是使用更好的种子。结果可能令人印象深刻。例如，改良的高粱品种产量可比常规品种高40%。基础设施很重要。世界银行在埃塞俄比亚的灌溉项目帮助农民将土豆产量从每公顷约8吨提高到35吨。

paragraphs.text: Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.
paragraphs.translation: 更好的技术也有帮助。肯尼亚的小咖啡农通过遵循一些简单的护理指南，如修剪掉除三根主茎外的所有枝条，能够将收入提高40%。许多邻居没有遵循建议，因为这看起来违反直觉。他们说，更多的茎应该导致更多的咖啡豆。然而，在看到遵循建议的人在一两个季节后获得更大收成后，许多其他人开始效仿。

paragraphs.text: One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.
paragraphs.translation: 传播知识的一种方式是将农场与他们的收获的大买家联系起来。当英国饮料巨头帝亚吉欧在肯尼亚西部建造一家啤酒厂时，它希望使用当地作物生产价格足够低廉的啤酒，以与非法自酿啤酒竞争。它组织农民成立团体，改善供应链以便他们获得种子和化肥，然后同意购买他们的粮食。它现在为约17,000名农民提供市场。其非洲业务负责人约翰·奥基夫表示，过去五年，该地区本地原材料的使用量已翻倍至约80%。

paragraphs.text: An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. "Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital," he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.
paragraphs.translation: 一个更重要的变化是从传统农业转向建立能够盈利地将技术和投资带给小农的企业。年轻的肯尼亚人泰塔·恩盖蒂奇在学习工程时想赚点外快。他凑了20,000肯尼亚先令（约200美元）来种植西红柿。一切都出了问题。作物遭到害虫袭击。"然后一场大洪水吞噬了我们所有的资金，"他说。恩盖蒂奇先生坚持研究购买温室以保护植物免受虫害和雨水侵袭。最便宜的温室每间超过2,500美元，所以他设计了自己的，成本减半。很快，附近的农民开始向他下订单，现在他的公司Illuminum Greenhouses已售出超过1,400个温室，为约6,000人提供生计。业务不止于此；他还供应化肥、优质苗木和能提高产量的智能传感器。

paragraphs.text: Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.
paragraphs.translation: Illuminum的成功展示了技术如何帮助即使小型农场提高生产力。由于非洲如此大比例的人口以农业为生，即使生产率的小幅改善也能提升数百万人的收入。但从长远来看，小规模农业只能走这么远，尤其是在面对气候变化和人口压力时。

paragraphs.text: "If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education," says Mr. Ngetich. "Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there." Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.
paragraphs.translation: "如果我们真的想让人们摆脱贫困，就必须资助能让他们每月至少获得100美元收入的项目，以便他们能支付医疗和教育费用，"恩盖蒂奇先生说。"那些通过种植豆类或玉米每月额外给他们2美元的项目无法实现这一目标。"实现这些大跃升需要工厂和城市中的更好工作。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts.
paragraphs.translation: 共和党近几十年来的一个重大成功，是持续传播一个简单的经济增长公式：减税。

paragraphs.text: The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals.
paragraphs.translation: 这个公式并不奏效，但并未影响其受欢迎程度。尽管减税崇拜吸引了许多批评者，但它缺乏明显的竞争对手。

paragraphs.text: Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans.
paragraphs.translation: 民主党政治家倾向于以帮助那些被经济增长抛在后面的人为竞选主题。当民主党人确实谈论鼓励经济增长时，他们听起来往往像共和党人。

paragraphs.text: This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages.
paragraphs.translation: 这不仅是民主党面临的政治问题；也是美国的经济问题。国家需要一个关于经济增长驱动力的更好说法。近几十年的痛苦教训指向一个有希望的候选者：更高的工资。

paragraphs.text: Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks.
paragraphs.translation: 提高美国工人的工资应该是经济政策制定者的首要任务。我们都不必过于关注国家国内生产总值（GDP）增长的季度更新，而应专注于工人薪水的增长。

paragraphs.text: Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth.
paragraphs.translation: 暂时把关于更高工资的熟悉论点——公平性——放在一边。这里的论点是，更高的工资可以推动经济增长的引擎。

paragraphs.text: Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too.
paragraphs.translation: 也许最著名的受益例子是亨利·福特在1914年决定每天向他的T型车装配线工人支付5美元的故事。他这样做是为了增加生产——他支付溢价以维持可靠的劳动力。意想不到的收获是，福特的工厂工人也成了福特的客户。

paragraphs.text: The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more.
paragraphs.translation: 同样的逻辑仍然成立：消费驱动美国经济，收入更高的工人可以花更多钱。

paragraphs.text: Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces.
paragraphs.translation: 主流经济学家坚称，不可能强制实现可持续的工资增长，因为薪酬水平反映了市场力量的准确判断。

paragraphs.text: The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none.
paragraphs.translation: 传统观点认为，生产率增长是提高工资的唯一途径。从这个角度看，争取更高工资的努力适得其反。最低工资法会提高失业率，因为工资池中的资金有限，如果一些人得到更多，其他人就什么也得不到。

paragraphs.text: It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise.
paragraphs.translation: 正是在这种世界观背景下，主张减税将推动繁荣的观点变得流行。富人会投资，生产率会提高，工资会上涨。

paragraphs.text: In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind.
paragraphs.translation: 在现实世界中，事情更为复杂。工资受到雇主和工人之间拉锯战的影响，而雇主一直占上风。一个明显的证据是，自大约1970年以来，生产率增长和工资增长之间的差距不断扩大。生产率已经翻了一倍多；工资却远远落后。

paragraphs.text: A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote (矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.
paragraphs.translation: 关注工资增长将为减税魔力的诱人简单信念提供一种矫正方法（矫正方法）。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities.
paragraphs.translation: 期刊编辑决定哪些文章被发表，哪些不被发表，这影响着其他学者的职业生涯，并左右一个领域的发展方向。因此，人们希望期刊能尽一切努力建立一个多元化的编委会，以反映各种声音、经历和身份。

paragraphs.text: Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published.
paragraphs.translation: 不幸的是，《自然·神经科学》上的一项新研究读起来令人沮丧。研究团队发现，顶级心理学和神经科学期刊的大多数编辑是男性，并且居住在美国：这种情况可能加剧了该领域现有的性别不平等，并影响了被发表的研究类型。

paragraphs.text: Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers.
paragraphs.translation: 研究发现，男性占心理学期刊编辑的60%。在每一个资历级别上，男性编辑都显著多于女性编辑，并且在超过四分之三的期刊中，男性编辑占多数。至关重要的是，女性编辑的比例显著低于女性心理学研究人员的整体比例。

paragraphs.text: The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly.
paragraphs.translation: 在神经科学期刊中，这种差异更为明显：70%的编辑是男性，并且在88%的期刊中，男性占据大多数编辑职位。在这种情况下，女性编辑的比例并不显著低于从事神经科学研究的女性研究人员的比例——这一发现揭示了该领域更广泛的持久性别差异。

paragraphs.text: Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience."
paragraphs.translation: 基于他们的结果，研究团队得出结论：“在心理学和神经科学最受认可的学术期刊的编辑职位中，男性的想法、价值观和决策偏见被过度代表。”

paragraphs.text: Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty.
paragraphs.translation: 科学领域的性别不平等常被归因于资深学者更可能是男性的事实，因为历史上科学由男性主导：有人认为，随着时间推移，更多女性晋升到高级职位，该领域将变得更加平等。然而，这项研究表明，即使在心理学期刊的初级职位上，也倾向于由男性不成比例地占据，尽管实际上女性初级心理学教职人员多于男性。

paragraphs.text: This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers.
paragraphs.translation: 这表明，缺乏女性学者并不是问题所在。相反，女性在科学领域处于劣势有结构性原因。例如，女性薪酬较低，面临更大的育儿需求，这可能导致发表论文和获得资助较少——这些正是期刊在决定任命谁时所看重的因素。我们不应简单地将编委会的不平等归咎于传统，而应积极打破这些现有障碍。

paragraphs.text: A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.
paragraphs.translation: 期刊编辑中缺乏多样性也可能加剧心理学的WEIRD问题。如果期刊编辑主要是来自美国的男性，那么他们可能会更重视与西方男性人群相关的论文，无论是否有意识。

questionGroups.sourceText: 在中国，随着老龄化社会的到来，养老受到普遍关注。人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式。多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化。可以通过政府引导和社会参与，建立更多更好的养老服务机构，改进社区服务中心，鼓励居家自助养老，还可以推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式。随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加，养老设施将不断升级，服务质量逐步改进，老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适、健康快乐。

answer.modelTranslation: In China, with the advent of an ageing society, elderly care has attracted widespread attention. What people talk about most is what kind of elderly-care model should be adopted. Most people believe that the model needs to be diversified. Through government guidance and social participation, more and better elderly-care service institutions can be established, community service centres can be improved, and home-based self-care can be encouraged; a model that combines family care with social care can also be promoted. As the government and society keep increasing their investment in elderly-care services, care facilities will be continuously upgraded and the quality of service will be gradually improved, so that the lives of the elderly will become more convenient and comfortable, healthier and happier.
translationNotes: “老龄化社会的到来”译为 the advent of an ageing society，advent 比 coming 更书面。
“养老”根据语境译为 elderly care / elderly-care，避免逐字直译。
“养老模式需要多元化”用 needs to be diversified，体现被动与正式语体。
“政府引导和社会参与”译为 government guidance and social participation，名词化结构更地道。
“居家自助养老”译为 home-based self-care。
“家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式”译为 a model that combines family care with social care。
“持续增加投入”用 keep increasing their investment 表达持续性。
末句多个并列形容词用比较级 more...，healthier and happier 保持平行。
scoringPoints: ageing society / elderly care 等核心术语准确
被动语态与名词化结构使用恰当
“家庭养老与社会养老相结合”句式完整
末句并列比较级平行结构正确
整体时态（一般现在时与将来时）使用准确
